cells.tense: You are here with the pen, and the first stirring of feeling has room to move.
cells.act: hold the cloud of possible feeling without picking yet
cells.ask: When something pulls at you this week, don't name it and don't act on it. Let two days pass before you decide what it means.
cells.core:
Something is opening in the ending, and you're letting it open at its own speed. The first stirrings of what might come are here without your having to know what they mean, and you aren't rushing the clearing to make room faster — the gap where something was stays a gap a while, and what sits there can still change. That patience is doing work you haven't seen yet. It's how the new thing finds its place without being crowded.

Usually you decide sooner what a feeling means. Try staying with the not-yet-decided a little past your usual limit — that's what lets something real arrive before anything gets poured. So this week, when a pull comes, don't name it and don't act on it. Let two days pass before you decide. You get to feel what's actually there, and nothing has to be settled yet.

cells.tense: You're braced for an ending that hasn't arrived, and already writing the after.
cells.act: complete the form so it stands without you
cells.ask: Name the one form here that's already complete — the one that needs nothing from you to keep standing — and count only that as finished.
cells.core:
You're clearing the space before the thing in it has stopped moving. From where you stand it looks ended — you've already pictured the next room, the next name, the next arrangement — and the people still inside are mid-sentence. The bracing reads as readiness to you; from across the table it can land as being replaced while still speaking. You finish things ahead of their actual finish, and what gets called an ending is really a gap where something was still going.

It isn't more pushing that helps here — it's knowing which things are already done. So name the one form that is genuinely complete, the one that needs nothing from you to keep standing, and count only that as finished. Then act from there. A finished thing carries its own weight, and you move without dragging it behind you.

cells.tense: Something you shared ended, and you keep standing at the door that closed.
cells.act: let what was only possible stand finished
cells.ask: Give fifteen minutes to the smallest version of a thing you kept planning before the ending — a walk, a first paragraph — and nothing past that.
cells.core:
The thing is over and you haven't quite come inside. Its last arrangement still has a place you keep returning to — the same chair, the same hour — while the feeling that would tell you it's finished stays just out of reach. What was open is still open in you, and the closed thing and the live one are sharing space. You're past the door, and the door is what you keep describing.

What was only possible gets to stand finished by being done small. So give fifteen minutes — just that — to the smallest version of something you kept meaning to start before the ending: a walk around the block, a first paragraph, a first page. Nothing past that. While the old thing stays ended and unheld, you find out what's here by stepping into it a little.

cells.tense: You're letting something go — and not counting it as your own doing.
cells.act: return the favour at its true size
cells.ask: Take one offer that comes this week at the size it's actually given — no more, no less — and hand back exactly what the exchange calls for.
cells.core:
You're at the clearing. Something is being released — a ritual nobody renewed, an arrangement you keep keeping — and the hand letting go is yours, though if someone asked you'd say it just ran its course. The ending is being chosen and filed under things that happened. That gap is where the clearing sticks: nothing here gets credited to anyone, so nothing here can be released on purpose.

An ending needs an author, and authors are made by exchange. So take one offer at its real size — not smaller, not padded out — and give back exactly what it calls for, nothing performed on top. What comes back and what goes out stay level, and the letting-go gets a name on it.
